# TurnOver 2.0, build 21
### New to try
- TurnOver is free and open source: the code is at github.com/TurnOver-For-Mac/turnover, no tester key is needed any more, Send feedback opens TurnOver's problem form on GitHub, and Support TurnOver in the menu opens Ko-fi. - Plugins are back on for everyone: the TurnOver menu, Tools, Plugins. Shared as pull requests to the plugins repository, checked and reviewed before the library carries them. - TurnOver reads every app by default; VoiceOver still handles passwords and macOS's own prompts. Command Control Shift T gives the app in front to VoiceOver, or back to TurnOver, straight away (the layer's T still does too). - JAWS keys (Command Control Comma, then K, until you hear "JAWS keys"): JAWS's laptop layout with Caps Lock as the JAWS key. The reading grid (Caps U I O for lines, J K L for words, M comma period for characters, Y H N for sentences, Control U I O for paragraphs), Caps Shift J and L for the line up to and from the cursor, Caps Z for the virtual cursor, Caps F5 F6 F7 for the lists, Caps P and semicolon for the JAWS and PC cursors, Caps 8 and 9 to click, Caps Control H for speech history, Caps Control V for the app's version, Caps Control F12 for the time with seconds. During say all, Left and Right go back and on a sentence, and Page Up and Page Down change the speed for that say all. Every other key is the Windows style's.
### Fixed
- Waking the Mac at the lock screen no longer ends in several TurnOvers speaking at once: while the Mac is asleep, locked or just awake, a stuck voice is left to come back rather than restarted; a restart after a hang ends the stuck copy, so there is only ever one. Reported by a tester. - Giving a key to a command: the list of commands stays open for the next one; Escape leaves it. Reported by a tester. - Command Tab doing nothing until TurnOver was turned off and on: a modifier the Mac thought was still held is released before Command Tab passes, and the log records both states. - When the Mac's audio system hangs (it did for a few minutes on 20 Oct), TurnOver no longer hangs with it and restarts over and over: the fresh voice is built off the main thread, nothing waits on the speech queue, the device list is read on its own queue, and the log says which audio call stuck. - Screen recognition no longer freezes TurnOver (it could restart itself on a slow read). Reported by a tester.
- The Windows style (NVDA, Narrator and JAWS keys): no more pauses between the pieces of what TurnOver says ("Settings submenu 3 of 9", "OK button"), as NVDA says them. The Mac style keeps VoiceOver's way. Reported by a tester.

# TurnOver 2.0, build 20.2
### Fixed
- TurnOver restarting itself ("TurnOver's voice stopped"), most often after say all and an arrow key: the speech could wait for ever on the Mac's audio player. It no longer can, and if speech ever does stick, a fresh voice takes over within a few seconds instead of a restart. Reported by a tester. - Context menus: Right Arrow on an item with no submenu no longer closes the menu or freezes TurnOver, and Right on Open With opens it. Reported by a tester. - Word: every table in a document moves by row and column, not only the first. Reported by a tester. - Your own keys: VoiceOver's and NVDA's commands (next paragraph, next table and the rest) are listed whatever the keyboard style, and keys given to them work; right Option keys you set work with VoiceOver's Option Commander off. Reported by a tester. - Command Control Period switches TurnOver off and on again after an update; it had quit TurnOver instead.

# TurnOver 2.0, build 20.1
### Fixed
- The Dock, status menus and Spotlight: the arrows move through them again with a TurnOver app in front (in build 20 they went to the app behind).
